learning_outcomes.text: Explain when multiple cooperating agents beat a single agent and the costs they add
Compare orchestration topologies (supervisor, pipeline, peer network) and their trade-offs
Design message passing, shared state and hand-off protocols between agents
Assign roles and responsibilities so agents do not duplicate or contradict work
Diagnose failure modes such as loops, deadlock and runaway cost in multi-agent runs
Decide how to evaluate and observe a multi-agent system end to end

integrative_case: A company builds an incident-response assistant where one agent triages alerts, another investigates logs and a third drafts the postmortem: choose an orchestration topology, define hand-off contracts and shared state, cap total cost, and set up tracing so a stuck run can be diagnosed.
